summary: The hypothesis that a multi-heuristic MaxRects/skyline packer with randomized ordering search would score ≥80 was confirmed. The solution achieved a score of 94.82 out of 100 across the judge's 15 hidden test cases, well exceeding the prediction.
key_points: Score achieved: 94.82/100, exceeding the ≥80 prediction by ~15 points. This represents strong performance on the 2D rectangular knapsack problem with partial credit scoring.
The approach combined 6 item orderings × 3 MaxRects placement methods plus skyline packing and randomized search, all within the 1-second time limit per test case.

Remaining ~5 points of gap to perfect score likely come from suboptimal packing on tests with co-prime bin dimensions, supply-limited high-value items, or rotation-disabled cases where geometry constraints are tightest.
No feasibility issues were observed — the output JSON format, overlap checks, rotation constraints, and per-type limits all passed validation on all 15 tests.
